extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patentees, opponents, and patent attorneys involved in EPO appeal proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance on filing and prosecuting appeals before the European Patent Office Boards of Appeal, including who may appeal, timing, required contents, procedural steps, and likely costs and outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may file an appeal / party status
rubrics_metrics.description: Only a person who was a party to the first instance proceedings may appeal against a decision. Successors in title to a patent/patent application/party to the proceedings must be considered carefully as can have a big impact on the filing of an appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check that the appellant was a party at first instance; consider succession in title issues before filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adverse effect requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A party must be adversely affected by the decision in order to be able to file an appeal. The EPO takes this to mean that the decision must disagree with an explicit request of that party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm that the decision actually goes against an explicit request you made—mere dissatisfaction is not sufficient for standing to appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision requirement (appealable subject matter)
rubrics_metrics.description: The word 'decision' is important, as a document that does not decide anything cannot be appealed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the document you intend to challenge is a formal decision; non-decisional documents are not appealable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of appeal – time limit
rubrics_metrics.description: Notice of appeal from a decision must be filed within two months from the date the decision is notified. This is the date on the letter from the EPO, plus the EPO’s ten day postal rule. This time period is not extensible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute the deadline as letter date + 10 days. The two-month period cannot be extended—late filing means the appeal is deemed not to have been filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of appeal – required contents
rubrics_metrics.description: A notice of appeal must detail the name and address of the party filing the appeal, and set out in brief the decision being appealed and the extent of the appeal (for example all or part of the decision).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include clear identification of appellant, contact details, which decision is appealed, and whether the appeal is in respect of all or part of that decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of appeal – fee and effect of non-payment
rubrics_metrics.description: The notice of appeal carries an official fee, and both the fee and the notice of appeal must reach the EPO before the deadline or the appeal is deemed not to have been filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure payment of the official fee on time; otherwise the appeal will be rejected as not filed. Reduced official fee applies for private individuals and certain non-profits (e.g., universities).

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of grounds – time limit
rubrics_metrics.description: The notice of appeal must be supported by a statement of grounds, which must be filed within four months from the date the decision is notified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: File a fully developed grounds statement within four months; do not rely on filing only a short indication that the decision is wrong.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of grounds – content standard
rubrics_metrics.description: It is important to set out as full a case as possible initially. It is not sufficient to simply state that the decision is wrong – legal and factual reasons why the decision should be set aside must be included.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide legal and factual arguments and evidence supporting each contention; incomplete grounds risk non-admissibility or weaker prospects of success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admission of new arguments, amendments and prior art on appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: New arguments, amendments and even prior art can be raised on appeal but the Board of Appeal will always determine whether these should be admitted and fairness to all parties is something that they have to consider.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be prepared that the Board may exercise discretion to admit or exclude late-filed matter; justify admission and address fairness to other parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inter partes dynamics and amendments when patentee is non-appealing
rubrics_metrics.description: In inter partes proceedings, if only one party appeals (e.g. the opponent), then the other party will be automatically joined in the appeal proceedings and will be entitled to respond. However, where the patentee is the non-appealing party, the patentee will not be permitted to make amendments to the claims during appeal that would put them in a better position than before the appeal was filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you are the non-appealing patentee, do not expect to be able to amend claims to gain a better position; if you are the appellant, expect the other party to be joined and to have opportunity to respond.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial review by the division (interlocutory revision)
rubrics_metrics.description: The division that made the decision under appeal (e.g. the Examining Division) will review the appeal initially, and their own decision. If the appeal addresses all of the issues that lead to their adverse decision, that division can allow the appeal and overturn the earlier decision (known as interlocutory revision).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An interlocutory revision can dispose of the appeal without referral to the Board if the division considers all issues addressed; drafting grounds to clearly cover the division's objections may prompt such a revision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board assessment – admissibility and allowability
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board of Appeal will assess both the admissibility and the allowability of the appeal. If the appeal does not meet the minimum formal requirements (e.g. if the appeal fee was not paid in time) then it will be rejected without substantive review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Satisfy formal requirements precisely (timely fee, proper notice, grounds within time, etc.) to avoid summary rejection; admissibility is a threshold issue separate from substantive merits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enlarged Board of Appeal referral scope and effect
rubrics_metrics.description: Occasionally, a Board of Appeal will refer a question to the Enlarged Board of Appeal. The enlarged board is not a higher instance court as such, and a referral should not be thought of as a further avenue for appeal. The enlarged board is only able to decide questions relating to the uniform application of law, or the interpretation of law, and not questions relating to the particular issues of a case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand that referral suspends appeal proceedings until the Enlarged Board answers the question; referral addresses legal uniformity/interpretation only, not case-specific facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunity to file observations and Board opinions
rubrics_metrics.description: If the appeal is deemed admissible then the Board of Appeal 'shall invite the parties, as often as necessary, to file observations'. This usually means the Board will send the applicant an opinion on the appeal, and the applicant will be given an opportunity to comment on the Board’s opinion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect to receive one or more opinions from the Board and be given chances to file observations; costs can vary depending on complexity and whether the opinion favours the appellant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oral proceedings – request, written procedure, and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Appeal proceedings will usually terminate in an oral hearing if one or both of the parties has requested oral proceedings. However, the proceedings can take place entirely in writing if both parties agree. The Board may issue further opinions before summoning the applicant to oral proceedings, or may issue a summons immediately after the first opinion. A number of years can therefore pass between filing the initial notice of appeal and a date being scheduled for an oral hearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decide whether to request oral proceedings; be prepared for lengthy lead times and for written exchanges prior to any hearing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceleration of proceedings – legitimate reasons required
rubrics_metrics.description: Proceedings can be accelerated but only if the applicant can give a legitimate reason why acceleration might be preferable. For example, a pending infringement action might be considered to be a legitimate reason.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you need acceleration, document a legitimate reason (e.g., parallel litigation) when requesting expedited treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written submissions prior to oral proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: If oral proceedings are requested, written submissions may be filed prior to the proceedings taking place.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: File thorough written submissions in advance; typical preparation cost range provided in the guide.

rubrics_metrics.name: Costs estimates for stages of appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimated costs: first-stage (notice) ~£2,000–£2,500; preparing/filing grounds ~£2,000–£8,000; commenting on Board's opinion £0–£5,000; written submissions prior to oral proceedings £1,000–£5,000; attending oral proceedings £3,000–£10,000. Total typical appeal cost ~£10,000–£35,000 (typical £15,000–£20,000), often spread over up to 4 years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these figures for budgeting and planning, noting wide ranges depending on complexity; dollar equivalents provided (~$15k–$55k total).

rubrics_metrics.name: Final decision powers of the Board
rubrics_metrics.description: Once the Board of Appeal feels all issues have been considered fully, it will issue a final decision. The Board has the power to grant any remedy that could have been granted by the Division whose decision is under appeal (such as grant or refusal of a patent application).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Board's decision is final within the EPO appeal system; plan strategy accordingly since there is no further internal EPO appeal beyond the Board (except limited referrals to the Enlarged Board on points of law).

rubrics_metrics.name: Costs allocation between parties
rubrics_metrics.description: Each party usually pays its own costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not expect routine recovery of opponent's appeal costs; budget for each party bearing its own expenses.
